columns.typeText: ColumnDef<{ rowSelectionFeature: TableFeature; rowSortingFeature: TableFeature; rowPaginationFeature: TableFeature; sortedRowModel: (table: Table<any, any>) => () => RowModel<any, any>; paginatedRowModel: (table: Table<any, any>) => () => RowModel<any, any>; }, TData>[]

x-gts-traits.intent: Render tabular data with sorting, optional row selection, and pagination from one columns/data pair.
typical_uses: Tabular data with more rows than fit on one screen, where the user sorts a column
A list the user selects rows from for a bulk action
Paged results the user steps through instead of scrolling one long list

dont_use_when.situation: Static markup with no sorting, selection or pagination need

invariants.text: `columns` and `data` are both generic over the same `TData` - a `ColumnDef` built for one row shape used against a `data` array of a different shape is a type error at the call site, not a runtime contract this schema can assert.

`enableRowSelection` alone makes rows selectable and turns on the footer's "N of M row(s) selected" text; it renders no checkbox column by itself. A checkbox column only appears when `columns` also includes one built with `dataTableSelectionColumn()`.

`pageSize` seeds and live-resyncs the internal pagination state; zero or negative values make the page-index rescale on prop change (`current.pageIndex * current.pageSize / pageSize`) divide by zero or go negative, so it must stay a positive integer.

Sorting, row-selection and pagination state are internal, not props: `sorting`/`rowSelection`/`pagination` are component-owned useState, never lifted to DataTableProps, so there is no way to preset or control them - "DataTable is sortable/selectable/paginated" is discoverable only from `columns`' own fields and `enableRowSelection`. A consumer needing controlled state builds against `useTable` directly (see the dataTableFeatures companion).

anti_patterns.dont: Mix column defs built against different TFeatures objects in one `columns` array
anti_patterns.do_instead: Build every column with `dataTableColumnHelper()` (or a hand-rolled helper bound to the same `dataTableFeatures`), never a mix

anti_patterns.dont: Set `enableRowSelection` and expect a checkbox column to appear on its own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Include `dataTableSelectionColumn()` in `columns` explicitly - the flag and the column are independent opt-ins

good.title: Sortable, selectable, paginated table

bad.title: enableRowSelection with no selection column
bad.why: Without a column built by `dataTableSelectionColumn()` in `columns`, rows become internally selectable (the footer count can change) but nothing in the rendered table lets a user actually select one - the flag and the column are independent opt-ins, and this omits the second one.

slots.description: Column definitions - what data each column reads, how its header and cells render, and whether it participates in sorting. The one required way to shape what DataTable renders.

capabilities.name: row_selection
capabilities.description: Rows become selectable and the footer reports "N of M row(s) selected", enabled by @tanstack/react-table's rowSelectionFeature - one of the three features dataTableFeatures registers. The checkbox column is a separate opt-in: it appears only when `columns` also includes one built with `dataTableSelectionColumn()`.

companions.description: A createColumnHelper pre-bound to DataTableFeatures - the one column helper every DataTable column def should be built with.
Ready-made row-selection column (checkbox header/cell) a consumer spreads into `columns` to opt into selectable rows.

The fixed TanStack Table v9 feature set DataTable registers - row selection, row sorting, row pagination. Not configurable per instance; a consumer needing a different feature set (filtering, column visibility, grouping, ...) builds directly against `useTable` with this set as the starting point (see data-table.md's Escape hatch).
